patterns.note: The page is structured as a continuous vertical scroll, with each distinct typeface example occupying a large, full-width section that centers itself visually as it comes into focus during scrolling.

The primary content consists of extremely oversized, expressive display typography, showcasing various font families, contrasted with minimal, small-scale sans-serif text for navigation and copyright.
A high-contrast, two-color scheme dominates, featuring a vibrant, almost neon orange background with deep forest green text, creating a bold and energetic visual impact.

The site employs a simple, native vertical scroll without any scroll-triggered animations, parallax effects, or sticky elements; all content, including the header logo and navigation, scrolls off-screen.
Each font demonstration acts as a distinct, full-viewport-height section, presenting the font name in its own style, creating a rhythmic visual progression down the page.

technique_notes: The site is built as a single, long-scrolling page where each major content block (a font example) is designed to fill the viewport vertically. The background color is a static, full-bleed element. Content simply scrolls into and out of view without any dynamic reveal animations or sticky header behavior.
The motion system is entirely based on the browser's native scroll behavior, with no custom scroll-triggered animations or transitions applied to elements as they enter or exit the viewport.

design_tokens.type_scale: Extremely oversized display headings (often filling the screen) are the primary content, with very small, subtle sans-serif text used for navigation and copyright information.
design_tokens.spacing: airy — very generous vertical spacing between large typographic examples, creating a sense of individual presentation for each font.

standout: This site stands out by making the typography itself the entire visual experience. It's a bold, almost brutalist showcase of fonts, using an extremely high-contrast color palette and minimal UI to put the expressive typefaces front and center, rather than relying on typical marketing layouts or complex interactions.
